overview: AoFrio Limited (formerly Wellington Drive Technologies, renamed September 2022) is a New Zealand-headquartered, NZX-listed hardware-enabled SaaS company that designs and manufactures energy-efficient electronically commutated (EC) motors and fans, and IoT-enabled smart controllers/cloud connectivity (SCS Connect, SCS 800, AoFrio iQ) for commercial refrigeration in the food and beverage industry, principally bottle coolers used by Coca-Cola, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo and other beverage brands and their bottlers. The company operates two reporting segments, Motors and IoT, sells globally with heavy concentration in the Americas (LATAM and increasingly USA), and is pursuing diversification into Food Retail and Chilled/Frozen Food adjacent markets.

business_model.summary: Revenue is split between hardware sales of EC motors/fans (commoditized, lower margin, largely transactional) and IoT hardware plus recurring multi-year cloud data/software connection fees (higher margin, increasingly recurring). FY25 revenue was NZ$83.2m (+4.4% YoY): IoT NZ$47.1m (+8.9%, 42.5% gross margin) and Motors NZ$36.1m (flat, 17.7% gross margin). Recurring SaaS/data revenue was only 3.8% of FY25 revenue recognized ($3.2m) against a long-term target of 50%, with $17.8m of contract liability (deferred revenue) on the balance sheet to be recognized over 1-10 year contracts as the installed base of connected devices (3.2m at FY25 year-end, +22% YoY) converts to recognized revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Recurring cloud/SaaS revenue (subset of IoT, recognized)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - enterprise, concentrated among global beverage bottlers/brands (Coca-Cola system bottlers, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo), OEMs, and USA appliance/water-heater manufacturers; four customers each individually >=10% of FY25 revenue together accounted for 49% of Group revenue ($40.5m of $83.2m), all within the Americas segment (up from two customers/27% in FY24)
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas 84.7% (LATAM plus growing USA), APAC 8.3%, EMEA 7.0% (FY25); North America growth driven by ECR2 motors into water heaters/supermarket display units and early SCS IoT launch; South America (core CDE/LATAM base) revenue declined 12.5% YoY on reduced demand

main_competitors: Generic/local EC motor and fan manufacturers (especially in EMEA on price)
In-house/legacy telemetry and asset-tracking vendors for cooler fleets
Traditional AC-motor incumbents being displaced by EC technology
competitive_position.market_position: Long-established, high-share incumbent supplier of EC motors/fans and connected controllers to the global cold drink equipment (CDE)/bottle cooler market, particularly strong in LATAM; a much smaller, earlier-stage challenger in IoT-enabled fleet SaaS platforms versus larger industrial IoT and cold-chain software players

moat_factors.description: SCS/Monitor/Click devices installed on coolers create a base of ~3.2m connected devices and long-dated (1-10 year) data contracts, generating switching costs once fleets are connected and integrated into customer operations

Decades-long relationships with global beverage brands and bottlers (Coca-Cola system, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo) and high customer NPS (+62, up 9pts) support renewal and cross-sell, though this coexists with severe customer concentration risk

ECR2 motor technology delivers validated energy savings (up to 68% in bundled configurations) that align with customer ESG targets and evolving efficiency regulations (e.g., US DOE water heater standards), supporting product pull-through
Growing connected fleet (3.2m devices, app utilisation up 31%) improves AoFrio iQ's fleet insights and product value, but platform is nascent (10 pilot customers) and unproven at scale
Micro-cap scale (~NZ$30-70m market cap) limits R&D budget, negotiating leverage and resilience versus larger diversified industrial competitors

weaknesses: Motors segment is a commoditized, price-competitive, low-margin (17.7%) business exposed to aggressive competitor pricing (notably in EMEA) and tariff-driven customer reshoring
Extreme customer concentration: four customers = 49% of FY25 revenue, all in the Americas, including a single largest USA motor customer (~US$5.6m FY25 revenue) now onshoring supply to avoid tariffs
Recurring/SaaS revenue still tiny (3.8% of revenue) relative to the 50% long-term target; AoFrio iQ and SCS 800 are pre-commercial/early trial stage
Sub-scale balance sheet: net debt rose to $8.2m (from $2.5m) and cash fell to $1.3m at FY25 year-end, funding growth partly via extended supplier payment terms and increased trade finance facility

growth_drivers: Commercial launch of SCS 800 cellular-connected controller (targeted May 2026) opening USA/Europe/Canada markets with a combined TAM of ~700,000 units/year where cellular is the preferred standard

AoFrio iQ SaaS platform (AI-enabled fleet management) moving from 10 pilot customers toward broader commercial availability targeted Q3 FY26, intended to lift recurring/SaaS revenue toward the 50% long-term target

Diversification into adjacent verticals: first Food Retail customer secured (NZ convenience store chain, 115 sites), a Chilled/Frozen Food (pet food) customer (~3,500 freezers), and an ice-cream vertical proof-of-concept in Chile showing equipment-loss reduction from 20% to 0.5%
New fan pack sizes (7", 8", 9", 10") and new motor applications (e.g., ECR2 into beverage-dispenser agitators) protecting/expanding Motors margin and unit volumes

Two-path FY26-FY30 growth strategy presented at December 2025 Investor Day: self-funded path targeting ~10% revenue CAGR to ~$140m/EBITDA $14m by FY30, versus an externally-capitalized 'aspirational' path targeting >3x revenue to $300m and EBITDA of $50m by FY30 - now partly being funded via the May 2026 capital raise
Secular tailwind from cold-chain energy efficiency, refrigerant/ESG regulation, and increasing enterprise appetite for connected/AI-driven asset management across cooler fleets

business.description: Four customers represent 49% of FY25 revenue (up from two customers/27% in FY24), all in the Americas; loss or reduction of any one materially impacts results, as already evidenced by the largest USA motor customer's decision to onshore supply in FY26
Motors and Fans is a lower-margin (17.7%), price-competitive category facing aggressive competitor pricing, particularly in EMEA where revenue fell 8.8% YoY

business.risk: Execution risk on new product/SaaS launches
business.description: Growth thesis depends heavily on SCS 800 and AoFrio iQ converting from pilot/trial stage to meaningful commercial revenue within the next 12-24 months; delays have already occurred (diversification 'progressed at a measured pace' in FY25 versus plan)

business.risk: Product obsolescence / long sales and qualification cycles
business.description: OEM/bottler capital purchase cycles are multi-year; new hardware must pass customer qualification programmes, slowing revenue realization from new launches

financial.risk: Rising net debt and tight liquidity
financial.description: Net debt increased from $2.5m to $8.2m and cash fell to $1.3m at 31 Dec 2025; working capital pressure from longer customer payment terms, higher inventory and increased reliance on extended supplier payment terms (contract manufacturer East West) and an enlarged $10m trade finance facility

Company has posted statutory net losses every recent year (FY25 loss $2.1m, FY24 loss $1.9m); FY25 annual report and H1-25 interim both include explicit going-concern assessments dependent on Board-approved 2026 budget assumptions and continued bank trade facility support (at least $10m for 12+ months); no going-concern qualification currently exists but the disclosure signals financial fragility for a micro-cap

May 2026 placement (65.1m shares at NZ$0.07 to Wairahi Investments, raising $4.6m) plus a subsequent 1-for-7 renounceable rights issue at the same $0.07 price materially dilutes existing holders; share count has grown from ~431.9m (FY24) toward >500m post-raise; further dilution likely if the more capital-intensive 'aspirational' growth path is pursued

Functional currency is USD but presentation currency is NZD; FY26 guidance assumptions are based on a 0.606 NZD/USD rate and management explicitly flags an expected NZD strengthening as an adverse headwind to reported revenue and profit

regulatory.description: April 2025 US reciprocal tariffs directly reduced Q4-25 US motor demand and drove the company's largest USA motor customer (~US$5.6m FY25 revenue) to onshore supply away from AoFrio's Vietnam-manufactured ECR2 motors, with FY26 mitigation still being negotiated
Reliance on a Vietnam-based contract manufacturer (East West) for motor production creates exposure to further shifts in US trade policy toward Vietnam-origin goods
Changing regulatory standards (e.g., finalized US DOE water heater efficiency standards) can be a tailwind (driving ECR2 motor adoption) but also a compliance cost and uncertainty factor

macro.description: Broader macroeconomic headwinds from US tariff policy caused 'more subdued customer capital spending than anticipated' across several regional markets in H1-25 and continue to cloud FY26 guidance, which management has declined to quantify
Bottler/OEM capital purchase cycles are discretionary and can be deferred in a weaker macro environment, directly affecting AoFrio's hardware sell-through
Rising bank borrowings and trade finance usage make the company sensitive to interest rate levels; finance costs increased $0.3m in FY25 due to increased borrowings and extended payment terms

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Commercial refrigeration / cold drink equipment is a mature, essential replacement-and-growth market with a structural shift toward energy-efficient EC motor technology and IoT-enabled fleet management, reinforced by ESG/carbon-reduction targets among major beverage brands (refrigeration is ~35% of a cold drink's carbon footprint per company disclosure) and rising enterprise demand for connected asset management and AI-driven insights
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - revenue tied to customer capital expenditure cycles (bottler/OEM cooler fleet renewal and expansion) which can be deferred in weaker macro conditions or amid trade-policy uncertainty, as seen in H1-25/Q4-25
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - increasing use of bank trade finance and borrowings to fund working capital and growth investment means finance costs rise with base rates and facility utilization
key_input_costs: Electronic components and motor/fan raw materials (contract-manufactured in Vietnam)
Ocean freight/shipping (longer shipping times cited as a working capital driver)
Cloud/software engineering and R&D talent costs

recent_developments.event: FY2025 annual results released: record revenue of NZ$83.2m (+4.4%), EBITDA $3.5m (+$1.0m), gross margin 31.7% (+2.6pp), but revenue came in below the September 2025 updated guidance of ~$86m due to Q4-25 US tariff-driven motor demand weakness

Investor Day: management presented two FY26-FY30 growth paths - self-funded (~10% revenue CAGR to ~$140m/EBITDA $14m by FY30) versus an externally capitalized 'aspirational' path (>3x revenue to $300m, EBITDA $50m by FY30); several shareholders indicated support for the higher-growth path
AoFrio updated FY25 market guidance to revenue ~$86m and EBITDA ~$3.5m, subsequently missed on revenue due to tariff impact
Launched SCS 800 cellular-connected controller (June 2025) and commenced customer trials in the US and Europe; launched AoFrio iQ SaaS platform to early-adopter/pilot customers (10 by year-end)

Secured first Food Retail customer (NZ convenience store chain, 115 sites) and a Chilled/Frozen Food customer (pet food, ~3,500 freezers); largest USA motor customer's ECR2 motor volumes grew from 230,000 to 288,000 units even as tariff pressure mounted
Placement of 65,134,806 shares to Wairahi Investments Limited at NZ$0.07/share raising NZ$4.559m, described as the first stage of securing growth capital for the accelerated ('aspirational') strategy

Announced and executed a 1-for-7 pro-rata renounceable rights issue at NZ$0.07/share (opened 5 June, closed 18 June 2026) with an oversubscription facility, not underwritten, extending the capital raise to all eligible shareholders

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Results (February 2026) and H2-2025 earnings call

items.target: No specific numerical guidance provided; management expects revenue to exceed FY2025 levels ($83.2m) across all segments
items.notes: Management explicitly declined to give a guidance range given trade/tariff and NZD/USD currency volatility, calling FY26 an 'untraditional year' for guidance; this follows a FY25 guidance miss (revised guidance was ~$86m, actual was $83.2m)

items.target: Expected improvement over FY25's $3.5m, no specific number given
items.notes: Same caveats as revenue guidance regarding tariffs and FX
Management flags expected NZD strengthening against USD as an adverse headwind to reported (NZD) revenue and profit

items.target: 20% per annum revenue growth with 50% of revenue recurring (longer-term strategic goal, stated in FY25 annual report) — refined at Dec-2025 Investor Day into two explicit paths: ~10% CAGR self-funded to $140m FY30 revenue/$14m EBITDA, or an externally funded 'aspirational' path targeting $300m FY30 revenue/$50m EBITDA
items.notes: The Board is continuing to investigate options for capital to support the higher-growth path; May 2026 placement and rights issue are the first funding steps toward this
Undergoing final testing/certification as of FY25 year-end; early signs suggest faster-than-expected LATAM cellular adoption

items.target: Base solution commercially available Q3 FY26
items.notes: Currently in trial with 10 customers; pace of adoption expected to accelerate through 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Greg Balla described FY25 as 'an active and pivotal year' with successful launches of SCS 800 and AoFrio iQ, and expressed encouragement that LATAM cellular adoption is tracking faster than initially expected. Management acknowledged the largest USA motor customer's decision to onshore supply due to tariffs and is in discussions to mitigate the FY26 impact. On the earnings call, management defended the ~4% FY25 growth rate against analyst questioning about the case for additional capital investment, emphasizing execution quality (NPS +62) and strategic product positioning over near-term organic growth acceleration.

bull_case: Record FY25 revenue and EBITDA with material gross margin expansion (29.1% to 31.7%) show the mix-shift toward higher-margin IoT is working, and the 3.2m connected device base (+22% YoY) plus $17.8m of deferred revenue provide underlying momentum toward the long-term 50% recurring-revenue target

Two new growth product launches (SCS 800 cellular controller and AoFrio iQ SaaS platform) open a combined ~700,000-unit US/Europe TAM and position AoFrio to capture wallet share within an entrenched global bottler customer base with high satisfaction (NPS +62, up 9 points)

Clear, quantified management-articulated growth optionality (self-funded 10% CAGR to $140m or externally-funded 25% CAGR to $300m revenue by FY30) with shareholder support already indicated for the more aggressive path and initial capital (NZ$4.6m placement plus rights issue) now secured

Diversification into Food Retail and Chilled/Frozen Food verticals (first customers signed, strong proof-of-concept results such as 20%-to-0.5% equipment loss reduction in an ice-cream trial) reduces long-term dependence on the core CDE/bottle cooler market
Deep, multi-decade OEM/bottler relationships and proven energy-efficiency technology (up to 68% validated energy savings) align with customer ESG mandates, a durable secular tailwind
bear_case: Severe and worsening customer concentration (four customers = 49% of FY25 revenue, up from two/27% in FY24) creates outsized single-customer risk, already crystallizing as the largest USA motor customer onshores supply in FY26 due to tariffs

Deteriorating balance sheet: net debt roughly tripled to $8.2m and cash fell to $1.3m in FY25, funded partly through extended supplier payment terms and an enlarged trade facility, alongside going-concern disclosure language and a persistent statutory net loss track record

Meaningful shareholder dilution already underway (May 2026 placement plus 1-for-7 rights issue at NZ$0.07/share, both below prior trading levels) with more likely if the company pursues its externally-funded 'aspirational' growth path

Motors segment remains commoditized and margin-thin (17.7% gross margin) with EMEA revenue declining on aggressive competitor pricing, while core recurring-SaaS revenue is still just 3.8% of total revenue versus a 50% aspiration that remains years away

Management has twice missed or withdrawn guidance in the past year (FY25 revenue came in below the revised $86m guide; FY26 guidance range was withdrawn entirely) amid unresolved US tariff policy and unfavorable currency assumptions (NZD strengthening), underscoring low visibility for a thinly capitalized micro-cap
